summary: Donald Capps worked in religious studies. Educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and Chicago, he held posts at Oregon State, Chicago, UNC Charlotte, Phillips University, and was William Harte Felmeth Professor of Pastoral Theology at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

A scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies, Donald E. Gjertson earned his PhD at Stanford under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda. He taught at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from circa 1976 to 2011.

Donald K. Swearer worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and later served at Harvard University as a Distinguished Visiting Professor (2004–2010) and Distinguished Visiting Fellow (~2004–2012).

Donald Keene specialized in Japanology, studying at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (from 1955).

Philosopher Donald Phillip Verene earned his BA from Knox College and his doctorate from Washington University in St. Louis. He served as Chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College and Sapienza University of Rome.
Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle, and Ludo Rocher.

A scholar of Buddhist and Tibetan studies, Donald S. Lopez Jr. earned his degrees at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He taught at Middlebury College (~1979–1989) before joining the University of Michigan in 1990.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dongak Tendzin was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, while also teaching Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Buddhist studies figure Dongchu studied at Minnan Buddhist Academy under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute (~1944–1949) and abbot of Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949), and founded the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Culture (1955).

Dongmei Fang was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later teaching at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Archaeologist and historian Donna C. Kurtz studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College, Oxford. She held a position at the Classical Art Research Centre from circa 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista worked in Tibetology. Educated at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus, he was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1993) and served on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Indologist Doranne Jacobson earned a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

A scholar of Indology and archaeology, Doris Meth Srinivasan studied at Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania. She held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, George Mason, and as a curator at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen.

Dorje Tseten was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a degree in education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948) and served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Federal University, he completed his doctoral dissertation under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (~1842–1846).
